```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days, not scale. Brief A shows paid-only entry points in the cheap tier (ExpirationOps is a 14-day trial, then $49/mo; NeverFined starts at $29/mo). Brief B shows three of six competitors giving free tiers that cover most small merchants (Zigpoll free to 50 responses, Compra free to 100, Fairing free to 200 orders/mo). That makes converting a first customer to paid harder in B.",
    "A's buyer has a concrete financial reason to pay: penalties and missed renewals. Its three Reddit demand quotes come from different roles (solo engineering firm owner, HR practitioner, therapist), all describing multi-state renewal pain. B's demand evidence is a single Reddit thread.",
    "A's competitors charge $500–800/location/yr for tracking plus filing, and enterprise tools run $3,999–10,000+/yr. The market pays well above the entry tier, so a narrow, better-maintained tracker has room to charge.",
    "B's own case against says merchants expect reviews, ranking, and trust signals (SOC2/ISO) before granting access to order and customer data. A zero-review app built in six weeks has none of these. A can be sold directly to a narrow niche without marketplace reputation.",
    "B's strongest point, Zigpoll's $125K MRR as a solo founder, cuts both ways. The same brief says it took two years and a founder with two prior SaaS exits. That is weak support for a 90-day first sale.",
    "A carries real risks of its own. Paid search costs more ($10–14.50 CPC vs about $6 in B). Continuous rule-change data maintenance is a burden. Some of A's demand quotes concern professional licensure rather than business licensure. These lower confidence but do not flip the pick."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand rests on one Reddit post. The brief claims this post shows 'existing willingness to pay for an automated tool' only because the merchant tried and gave up on calling customers. Abandoning manual outreach does not show willingness to pay, especially when free tools covering that need already exist. The supporting Zigpoll origin story is flagged as a seed quote and comes from a competitor, not an independent buyer.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with no clear wedge, and neither offers direct evidence that a new entrant could win a first paying customer. A wins mainly because its market has no visible free tier, its buyers face penalty-driven urgency, and it does not depend on marketplace reviews. Its higher paid-acquisition costs and data-freshness burden are real risks."
}
```
